name: Halverson Synth-Wool Formal Blazer (Aug-Cut)
description:
Halverson's mid-range blazer in their standard synth-wool blend — a fabric that reads as professional without the cost of genuine animal-fiber wool. The Aug-Cut variant adds a structured right-shoulder seam that opens along a concealed magnetic closure, allowing access to shoulder-mount chrome without removing the jacket. The left cuff has a discreet port-access panel sized for the three most common BCI tether standards. Neither modification is advertised on the label; they're listed in the technical spec sheet available at point of sale.

This is the blazer a Tier 2 worker buys when they get a Tier 3 job offer and need to dress for the interview before they can afford Tier 3 clothes. It holds up to regular dry-cleaning cycles, drapes cleanly, and photographs well. The construction is honest — not luxurious, but not pretending to be.
cultural_context: Halverson occupies the aspirational middle — clothes that signal effort and seriousness without signaling wealth. Wearing a Halverson Aug-Cut blazer to a corporate interview tells the interviewer you're augmented, you're functional, and you're not trying to hide it. That reads differently depending on which Corponation is interviewing you.
story_hooks: The character bought this blazer for a Tier 3 interview five years ago and has worn it to every significant event since. It's been dry-cleaned so many times the synth-wool has a slightly different texture at the lapels. They're considering whether to replace it or keep wearing the history.

A Halverson quality-control recall notice comes through: a batch of Aug-Cut magnetic closures was produced with a micro-current flaw that can interfere with older shoulder-mount chrome. The character's blazer is in the affected batch.
Someone at a Tier 4 event comments on the blazer — not unkindly, but precisely enough that the character understands they've been identified as not belonging.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sharp, structured blazer with clean lines and subtle professional geometry. The right shoulder bears a nearly invisible seam that breaks the traditional jacket silhouette—evidence of engineering rather than pure tailoring. Sits with quiet confidence on the frame, neither oversized nor aggressively fitted. The overall impression is competent, purposeful, and deliberately transparent about its wearer's augmentation status.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not restrictive. Shoulders sit squared and defined. Sleeves taper slightly toward the wrist without binding. The right shoulder panel sits fractionally looser to accommodate chrome or articulated joints beneath. Torso follows the body without clinging. Cut for movement and layering over tech-wear.
physical_description.primary_material: Synth-wool blend (70% synthetic polymer, 30% recycled natural fiber). Matte finish with subtle surface memory. Resists wrinkles and staining without the cost or maintenance of genuine wool.
physical_description.texture: Smooth to the touch with a soft nap that catches light slightly. Crisp at the seams and edges. The aug-access panels are seamlessly woven—no perceptible texture difference, but the fabric weight is fractionally denser in those zones.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray as primary (Halverson's signature neutral). Single-stitch detailing in muted silver along the interior of the aug-cut seam. Lining in black synthetic with subtle geometric grid pattern (functional—helps with wear visibility and thermal regulation).
physical_description.closures: Two-button front closure (mother-of-pearl-effect polymer, not genuine). The concealed right-shoulder magnetic closure is invisible from outside. Left cuff port-access panel secured by four small friction-fit snaps that blend into the cuff stitching.
distinctive_features: Left cuff BCI tether port panel (three-standard compatible)
Reinforced shoulder and upper-back paneling (supports weight of chrome)
Internal chest pocket with RFID-blocking weave
Silver-tone Halverson & Crane woven label, visible on interior
Wear-resistant patches at inner elbows and cuff edges
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2 aspirational / Tier 3 entry-level. The blazer signals ambition and augmentation readiness without claiming wealth.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by mid-tier corporate candidates, functional augmented professionals, and anyone betting on themselves. Not flashy enough to alienate conservative corpo sectors; augment-aware enough to signal you're integrated and not hiding modifications. A bridge garment—the outfit you wear when your paygrade is about to change.
physical_description.condition_typical: Immaculate when new or freshly dry-cleaned. Develops subtle scuffing at the cuffs and shoulder seams with regular wear. The magnetic closure may show faint wear marks around the edges after 6+ months of use, but remains fully functional. Creasing follows body contours naturally.
